title: POC scoping - model shortlist & benchmark plan (Glaciom Diagnostics)
summary: Initial POC scoping to pick 2-3 open models for a 4-week pilot. Discussed success metrics (F1 on entity extraction, latency targets), expected workload (qps and daily token volume), bench design (end-to-end and microbenchmarks), hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), timeline and next steps.
next_steps: Redwood to share POC cost estimate and security pack
Glaciom to provide 1 week of sample de-identified clinical notes and current inference logs
Schedule 30m benchmarking kickoff the week of Oct 4th
Agree on evaluation dataset and F1/EM targets
action_items: Avery Chen | Send POC pricing + security docs (SOC2, network diagrams) | 2027-10-01
Samir Patel | Upload 1 week of de-identified notes to shared S3 bucket (link in chat) | 2027-10-04
Marco Silva | Draft benchmark plan and open-model shortlist | 2027-10-03
Omar Idris | Share KMS/HSM requirements and compliance checklist | 2027-10-05
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-28 15:30 UTC — Duration 1:08:00 — Location: Zoom
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Dr Leila Rahman (Glaciom CTO), Samir Patel (Head of ML), Nina Gomez (Product), Omar Idris (Security), Tara Lim (Data Eng)

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, super excited — I'll run a quick agenda, then Marco will dive into benchmarking approach and model tradeoffs.
[00:10] Dr Leila Rahman: Great thanks. We wanted to, uh, make sure we get through the success criteria, cause we have a tight timeline for Q4.
[00:20] Marco Silva: Yeah, totally. Quick housekeeping: this call's being recorded for notes. I'll try to keep the deep perf slides short.
[00:35] Samir Patel: real quick — we're looking at two product flows: entity extraction from clinical consult notes and multi-lingual triage summarization — mostly en, es, and portuguese.
[00:50] Nina Gomez: And UX target is < 500ms median for short snippets, 95th <= 1.5s. But we care about accuracy more for the extraction task.
[01:05] Marco Silva: Noted. For the POC we usually recommend 2-3 model variants: a high-accuracy 7B/13B dense, a quantized 13B/16B variant, and a small 3-4B for throughput/budget comparison.
[01:20] Tara Lim: Quick question, when you say quantized, do you mean int8 or 4-bit? Our infra team prefers to avoid extreme quant unless validated.
[01:30] Marco Silva: Good call — int8 / q4_0 are common; we'll test q4_0 and q8-ish paths as part of the bench to see quality delta.
[01:40] Dr Leila Rahman: Our keys: privacy (no PHI leaves the VPC), reproducible metrics, and explainability of entity labels.
[01:52] Omar Idris: Also: KMS integration for key rotation, audit logs for inference, and SSO/SAML for console access.
[02:05] Avery Chen: We'll include the Private deployment option — full VPC and KMS — in the security pack. For the hosted POC we can also run in a restricted region + dedicated tenancy if needed.
[02:18] Samir Patel: On workload sizing: current ingest is roughly 250k notes per month, average note size 800 tokens, peak qps approx 12 for real-time triage. Batch nightly processing is about 2M tokens overnight for ETL.
[02:38] Marco Silva: Ok so daily token volume ~ 6M tokens/day peak, roughly. That informs instance sizing and batching. We'll propose a bench matrix: latency microbench (single request p95), throughput bench (tokens/sec w/ batching), and end-to-end quality eval (F1 / Exact Match).
[02:58] Nina Gomez: For success criteria: extraction F1 >= 0.88 on our gold dataset; entity label accuracy verified by product SME; and latency p95 < 1.5s for median workload.
[03:10] Dr Leila Rahman: We also want to measure hallucination rate on summaries — maybe ROUGE and manual spot checks.
[03:20] Marco Silva: Makes sense. We'll include hallucination heuristics and a manual sample review step.
[03:30] Priya Nair: Timeline question — if we start first week of Oct, what's realistic for a 3–4 week POC?
[03:38] Marco Silva: Bench kickoff week of Oct 4th, two weeks for model benching + quality eval, then a one-week integration with your end-to-end pipeline — so 3-4 weeks total. We'll deliver a bench report + rollout recommendation.
[03:50] Samir Patel: What's the tester harness? Are you going to run locally or in our VPC?
[03:55] Marco Silva: Two phases: initial microbench in Redwood hosted infra for speed and parity, then run the selected candidates in your VPC (private) to validate KMS/latency. We can run the tests with a lightweight agent or via secure S3 inputs.
[04:10] Tara Lim: We need the tests to use our VPC subnets and NAT config — no outbound PHI.
[04:20] Avery Chen: We'll provide a network diagram and a temporary bastionless agent pattern; details in the security doc.
[04:28] Dr Leila Rahman: On model choices — open models only, we prefer not to use closed-source for regulatory reasons.
[04:36] Marco Silva: Right — shortlist candidates: LLaMA-3 style 13B (open checkpoint), Mistral 7B protein? sorry not protein — Mistral-7B open, and an instruction-tuned 16B variant like OpenX-16B (open) — plus a distilled 3B for throughput. We'll avoid vendor-locked models.
[04:56] Samir Patel: Can you run a multilingual variant? We have a decent Spanish + Portuguese corpus.
[05:02] Marco Silva: Yes — we'll include a multilingual fine-tuned candidate (XLM-derived or the open multilingual 13B). We'll run per-language evals and an aggregate metric.
[05:15] Nina Gomez: Any concerns about tokenization and medical abbreviations? We've seen tokenizers split up acronyms weirdly.
[05:22] Marco Silva: We'll add a tokenizer pre-check, and a small vocab-adapt step if needed; also KV cache behavior for long patient notes — we'll exercise long context performance because some notes hit 4k tokens.
[05:35] Tara Lim: Important: encryption at rest + in transit for cached KV data, and we need audit hooks.
[05:40] Omar Idris: Also retention policy — we want inference logs retained 30 days only.
[05:46] Avery Chen: All that is standard — security doc will specify retention config and how to scrub logs.
[05:52] Samir Patel: Bench metrics request: please include tokens/sec, GPU util, cost per 1M tokens, and a quality vs cost chart.
[05:59] Marco Silva: We'll produce a benchmarking spreadsheet with columns: model, instance type, quantization, median latency, p95 latency, tokens/sec (batched), GPU mem, cost estimate. Add F1/EM per test.
[06:15] Dr Leila Rahman: Would you recommend starting with a 13B dense or a quantized 16B? We're limited on budget but need solid F1.
[06:24] Marco Silva: Tradeoff: dense 13B usually gives better accuracy out of the box; quantized 16B may approach that with much lower cost but risk minor F1 regressions. We'll measure delta — typical delta ranges 1-4 points F1 depending on task.
[06:40] Samir Patel: If delta is >3 F1 points it's a no-go for us.
[06:45] Marco Silva: Understood — bench will flag any model >3 point drop vs baseline.
[06:50] Avery Chen: Who's the final decision maker on model choice?
[06:54] Dr Leila Rahman: Samir and I will decide with input from Nina. Security sign-off from Omar.
[07:00] Priya Nair: Good — I'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench kickoff and wrap.
[07:06] Marco Silva: One technical note — we'll instrument KV cache warm-up tests and continuous batching settings; these can materially lower per-token cost for nightly batch.
[07:18] Tara Lim: How do you measure hallucinations automatically?
[07:22] Marco Silva: For summaries we'll run factuality heuristics: NLI-based checks and token overlap plus manual spot checks; will report a hallucination rate metric.
[07:33] Samir Patel: For data privacy — can Redwood consume a synthetic subset instead of real PHI for initial bench?
[07:38] Avery Chen: Yes synthetic is fine for initial bench; for end-to-end we need de-identified notes.
[07:45] Dr Leila Rahman: Any pricing ballpark for the month-long POC (hosted vs private)?
[07:52] Avery Chen: Roughly: hosted POC ~ $8k-$12k for full bench across 3 models; private VPC POC ~ $15k-$25k due to reserved infra and KMS integration. We'll send a formal quote.
[08:04] Marco Silva: We'll also include a cost-per-unit table so you can estimate production run costs.
[08:10] Nina Gomez: Okay great. One last thing — can you include a small runbook for fallback model routing if a primary model fails?
[08:17] Marco Silva: Yep — we'll include recommended fallback policies: degrade to smaller model or route to dedicated infra with autoscale.
[08:25] Priya Nair: Recap and next steps: Redwood to share security pack, pricing, and benchmark plan by Oct 1; customer to provide sample notes and logs; schedule bench kickoff week of Oct 4.
[08:40] Dr Leila Rahman: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:46] Avery Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email and slack.

Notes / quick links: Security pack (placeholder): https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack/glac-2027 ; bench template: https://redwood.example.com/templates/bench-v2 ; shared S3 link (in chat).

End of transcript.
